raw_text:
12-week general fitness programme (post-MI, moderate-intensity only)
Overview and guardrails
- Intensity: Keep HR below 115 bpm and use RPE 3–4/10 (can talk in full sentences). If on beta-blockers or HR is unreliable, prioritize RPE and talk test.
- No breath holding: “Blow as you go” on every effort; avoid isometric holds and grinding reps.
- Stop immediately for any chest pain/pressure, unusual shortness of breath, dizziness, palpitations, unusual fatigue, or radiation to arm/jaw/back.
- Warm-up 8–10 minutes and cool-down 8–10 minutes every session.
- Frequency: 4 training days/week (2 aerobic-focused, 2 resistance-focused with brief low-intensity cardio), optional easy walking/mobility on other days.

Session building blocks (used throughout)
- Standard warm-up (8–10 min): 5–7 min easy cardio (RPE 2–3) + gentle mobility (ankle pumps, marching in place, shoulder rolls, thoracic rotations, diaphragmatic breathing).
- Standard cool-down (8–10 min): 5–7 min easy cardio back to RPE 1–2, then gentle stretches for calves, quads, hamstrings, chest, back (20–30 s each), and 2–3 min relaxed breathing.
- Balance and mobility finisher (5 min): tandem stance or single-leg stance near support (2 x 20–30 s/side), heel-to-toe walk 2 x 10 steps.

Cardio menu (choose any that keep HR ≤115): Treadmill walking (0–2% incline), recumbent/upright bike, elliptical (low resistance), rowing machine (light, smooth), indoor track walking. Use the talk test; keep cadence smooth.

Resistance training rules (machines/free weights/cables preferred over heavy barbells)
- Start light: RPE 3–4, 10–15 reps, 1–2 sets early on; progress to 2–3 sets by mid-program.
- Tempo: 2 seconds up, 2–3 seconds down; continuous breathing.
- Rest: 60–120 s between sets; longer if HR approaches cap.
- Exercise choices emphasize large muscle groups with joint-friendly patterns.

Resistance A (full-body, machine emphasis)
- Leg press or sit-to-stand to box: 1–3 x 10–15
- Seated row (cable or machine): 1–3 x 10–15
- Chest press machine: 1–3 x 10–15
- Step-ups to low box (hand support as needed): 1–3 x 8–12/leg
- Lat pulldown (wide or neutral grip): 1–3 x 10–15
- Seated hamstring curl: 1–3 x 10–15
- Pallof press (cable/band): 1–2 x 10–12/side
- Optional: standing calf raise 1–2 x 12–15

Resistance B (full-body, cable/free-weight light)
- Goblet squat or bodyweight sit-to-stand: 1–3 x 10–15
- One-arm cable row or machine row: 1–3 x 10–15/side
- Dumbbell incline press or machine chest press (light): 1–3 x 10–15
- Cable pull-through or hip hinge with dowel/light DBs: 1–3 x 10–12
- DB scaption or lateral raise (very light): 1–2 x 10–12
- Cable woodchop (high-to-low): 1–2 x 10–12/side
- Bird-dog or dead bug: 2 x 6–10/side
- Optional: biceps curl and rope pressdown 1 x 12–15 each (only if HR remains well within cap)

Progression principles
- Cardio time increases 3–5 minutes every 1–2 weeks while staying under HR cap and RPE 3–4.
- Resistance volume increases by either +1 set on key lifts or small load bumps (2–5%) when all reps are completed at RPE ≤4 and technique/breathing perfect.
- If HR drifts >115 or RPE >4, reduce speed/grade/resistance or extend rest.
- Reassess at Weeks 4 and 8: check resting HR, talk-test ease, exercise tolerance.

PHASE 1 (Weeks 1–4): Foundation and tolerance
Goal: Establish routine, perfect breathing, keep intensity clearly moderate. 4 training days/week.

Week 1
- Day 1 – Cardio steady
  - 8–10 min warm-up.
  - 15–20 min treadmill walk 0–1% incline at RPE 3 (HR ≤115).
  - 8–10 min cool-down + balance/mobility.
- Day 2 – Resistance A + easy cardio
  - Warm-up.
  - Each exercise 1–2 x 12–15 at RPE 3–4; 60–90 s rest; meticulous breathing.
  - Finish with 5–10 min easy bike walk (RPE 2–3) + cool-down/mobility.
- Day 3 – Cardio steady
  - 20 min bike or elliptical, RPE 3–4, HR ≤115.
  - Cool-down + balance/mobility.
- Day 4 – Resistance B + easy cardio
  - Same structure as Day 2: 1–2 x 10–15 each at RPE 3–4.
  - 5–10 min easy walk + cool-down.

Week 2
- Cardio: 22–25 min per cardio day.
- Resistance: Keep loads similar; where RPE <3, add a small load or 1 extra rep per set. Maintain 1–2 sets.

Week 3
- Cardio: 25–28 min per cardio day.
- Resistance: Move primary patterns (leg press, chest press, row, pulldown) to 2 sets; keep others 1–2 sets; RPE 3–4.
- Add 1 extra balance drill set if tolerated.

Week 4
- Cardio: 28–30 min per cardio day.
- Resistance: 2 sets for all main lifts; 60–90 s rest; ensure HR <115 throughout. Keep technique pristine.
- End-of-week light day option: 20–25 min easy walk (RPE 2–3) if feeling good.

PHASE 2 (Weeks 5–8): Build aerobic and strength volume
Goal: Gradually extend cardio to 30–35+ min; increase resistance to 2–3 sets while staying moderate.

Week 5
- Day 1 – Cardio steady: 30 min continuous (walk/bike/elliptical), RPE 3–4.
- Day 2 – Resistance A
  - 2 sets for all; if RPE ≤3 on set 2, add a third set to leg press and seated row next week.
- Day 3 – Cardio steady: 30–32 min alternate modality from Day 1.
- Day 4 – Resistance B
  - 2 sets for all; optional 1 isolation set if HR well below cap.

Week 6
- Cardio: 32–33 min each cardio day.
- Resistance: Add a third set to 2–3 compound moves (e.g., leg press, chest press, row). Keep RPE 3–4; extend rest to 90–120 s as needed.
- Technique/tempo check and breathing reinforcement.

Week 7
- Cardio: 33–35 min each cardio day.
- Resistance: 3 sets for primary patterns; 2 sets for accessories/core. If any set approaches RPE 5 or HR climbs, reduce load/reps.
- Add very gentle “varied pace” within HR cap: 3 min easy + 3 min moderate repeated, still ≤115 bpm.

Week 8
- Cardio: Maintain 35 min; try a different modality for joint relief.
- Resistance: Keep volumes from Week 7; introduce small load bumps (2–5%) on lifts where sets feel ≤RPE 3 and HR stays stable.
- Optional third light aerobic day (20–25 min easy walk) if recovery is good.

PHASE 3 (Weeks 9–12): Consolidate and add variety
Goal: Comfortably perform 35–45 min cardio most sessions; maintain 2–3 sets of 8–15 reps with smooth breathing and good control.

Week 9
- Day 1 – Cardio “steady with gentle undulation”
  - 36–38 min total: 6-min easy + 3-min moderate repeated x4 (never exceeding HR cap).
- Day 2 – Resistance A
  - 3 sets main lifts; 2 sets accessories; try 8–12 reps on one lower-body and one upper-body move if RPE remains 3–4.
- Day 3 – Cardio steady: 35–38 min alternate modality.
- Day 4 – Resistance B
  - Mirror Day 2; keep core and shoulder work light and controlled.

Week 10
- Cardio: 38–40 min both days; maintain gentle undulations (2–4-min easy/moderate blocks) within HR cap.
- Resistance: Keep 3 sets compounds, 2 sets accessories. If RPE drops ≤3, add 1–2 reps per set (still cap at 15) rather than load.

Week 11
- Cardio: 40–42 min per day. One day can be outdoors (flat route) to boost adherence; use HR monitor.
- Resistance: Slight variation to reduce monotony:
  - Swap leg press for step-up focus (3 x 8–12/leg) or machine squat pattern.
  - Swap chest press machine for DB incline (light).
  - Keep total set volume equal; RPE 3–4.

Week 12
- Cardio: 42–45 min per day, same intensity caps.
- Resistance: Maintain volumes; technique “audit” week—perfect tempo and breathing; no new load increases.
- End-of-week mini-reassessment: Note RPE at usual speeds, recovery HR after 1 minute of cool-down, perceived ease of talk test.

Example resistance loads and progress cues
- Start with loads that allow 12–15 reps at RPE ~3; stop with 2–3 reps “in reserve” and smooth breathing.
- When all sets land at RPE ≤3 for two consecutive sessions and HR response is unchanged, increase load 2–5% or add 1 rep per set (not both).
- If any set drives HR toward 115, pause, breathe, and resume with reduced load/reps.

Session structure by week (at-a-glance)
- Weeks 1–2: 2 cardio (20–25 min) + 2 resistance (1–2 sets of 12–15).
- Weeks 3–4: 2 cardio (25–30 min) + 2 resistance (2 sets; begin adding a third set to one or two big lifts).
- Weeks 5–6: 2 cardio (30–33 min) + 2 resistance (2–3 sets).
- Weeks 7–8: 2 cardio (33–35 min, gentle undulations) + 2 resistance (3 sets main, 2 sets accessories).
- Weeks 9–10: 2 cardio (36–40 min, undulations) + 2 resistance (3 sets main; rep ranges 8–15 as tolerated).
- Weeks 11–12: 2 cardio (40–45 min) + 2 resistance (maintain volume; focus on consistency and quality).

Recovery and monitoring
- Daily: Gentle walking on non-training days (10–30 min easy), mobility (5–10 min).
- Sleep: Aim 7–8 hours; avoid training when overly fatigued or ill.
- Hydration and timing: Sip water throughout; avoid large meals 1–2 hours pre-session; small carbohydrate snack if needed per comfort.
- Pre-session check-in: Energy level, medication timing, last symptoms. If unusual symptoms present, defer and monitor or seek guidance.
- Post-session: Record RPE peak, HR peak, any symptoms, and how quickly HR recovers in cooldown.

Safety notes
- Blood pressure and medications: If you have a cuff and clinic guidance, measure pre-session initially; coordinate with cardiology on any thresholds that should pause exercise.
- Avoid floor-to-stand transfers that spike effort; use benches and supports as needed.
- Environmental: Keep gym temps moderate; avoid hot, stuffy conditions.

This plan keeps intensity within cardiac rehab guidance, emphasizes breathing and pacing, and progresses volume gradually. If at any point tolerance lags (e.g., persistent fatigue beyond 24–36 hours, rising RPE at same workloads), hold or regress one week before progressing.
